title: Self-image as working self-description
content: An accumulated working picture of what kind of person one is can influence what one attempts and expects. The chapter attributes the picture to interpreted triumphs, failures, humiliation, and feedback, especially early-life experiences. The text describes the picture as a premise against which experience is judged.

title: Snap-back and self-confirming loops
content: Attempts to change a habit may falter when a familiar identity expectation persists. The author compares behavioral relapse with a rubber band returning to its original position and describes reinforcing cycles in which outcomes seem to prove an old identity.

thesis: Attempts to change a habit may falter when a familiar identity expectation persists.

terms.definition: Attempts to change a habit may falter when a familiar identity expectation persists.

author_mechanism: The author compares behavioral relapse with a rubber band returning to its original position and describes reinforcing cycles in which outcomes seem to prove an old identity.
conditions_and_limits: Avoid blame-laden interpretations of weight, eating or body appearance; no automatic relapse is inevitable.
application: After a setback, separate the event, strategy, interpretation and next attempt instead of inferring a permanent ceiling.
common_misreading: Treating a conceptual or anecdotal explanation as a universal causal law, without evaluating context, skills or competing explanations.
alternative_explanation: Habit cues, stress, skills, access, reinforcement and sleep can explain relapse without a self-image thermostat.
ethical_clinical_cautions: Avoid blame-laden interpretations of weight, eating or body appearance; no automatic relapse is inevitable.
substantive_paraphrase: Attempts to change a habit may falter when a familiar identity expectation persists.
